lines.latin: Shari' Mahmud Shanan Bek (Mahmoud Chanan Bey Street)

notes: Dark enamel plate at night, Alexandria; strong glare and a shadow band across the right half. The 'O' in MAHMOUD is damaged and reads as 'C' on the plate (transcribed as shown). Arabic is ligatured calligraphy; the dots of the first word are lost in the glare. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.
source_categories: Bilingual Arabic-French street signs in Egypt

author: effeietsanders
attribution: Photo: effeietsanders, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Flickr. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/9435171@N03/3442752366. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0/. Unmodified original.

lines.latin: 'ulwi (upper/overhead; fragment of the cropped top panel)

notes: Blue directional road sign in Luxor, slightly angled from below. English is misspelled on the sign ('Libarry', 'Intrnational') and is transcribed as written. Top edge is cropped: only 'Luxor Temple' and the Arabic fragment 'علوى' of the top band are visible (the Arabic name of the temple is not). Arabic uses Egyptian dotless final yaa ('الدولى'); the gap between 'مطار' and 'الأقصر' is very tight. No-horn and traffic-light pictograms below are distractors. Alternative query: 'Mubarak Library'.

author: Francisco Anzola
attribution: Photo: Francisco Anzola, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr. Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/10345599@N03/31109491468. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/. Unmodified original.
notes: Printed orange/yellow banner sign at upper left of a busy Islamic Cairo street scene, angled and only ~200 px wide (source is 1024 px). Not transcribed: a yellow strip of Arabic-Indic phone numbers and a partly cut bottom line ending '...الحاج: مصطفى عبد المحسن'; a portrait and a green logo at the left end. Distractors: blue plate 'احمد محمد سلطان ادريس' at upper right, cloth banners and bunting overhead.
